questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was definitely the academic and the language aspects of taking erasmus abroad that motivated me, but also the social one as this is completely imbedded in the two above mentioned qualities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was satisfactory and very interesting but unfortunately also limited in the sense that the educational, social and pedagogical parameters were not calibrated to a Master student on exchange. It is also worth noting that without my level of French, it would probably have been completely impossible to integrate with the system.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy, the websites and the course catalogues were hidden and the different deadlines and schedules were not very transparent - a more sophisticated work flow would have been much appreciated.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little assistance, and the administrative assistance was completely incompetent

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy in the sense that it was offered to students in Cité Universitaire, but of quite poor quality

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is expensive and difficult to find one, so if possible, try to team up with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was relatively easy, but it was complicated in the sense that both a digital application should be filled which in turn had to be sent as a printed out version to the administrative adviser at the host institution which seems completely ridicules.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My sending institution was rather helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend a good deal of time looking at the course catalogue that can usually be found in this mysterious website with multiple folders. Get the number of etcs and try to link these up with the UE. However, you are free to chose freely among the courses between the faculties - even more then 30 etcs points.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were very varied but generally at a lower level in an academic sense. Repetition and description was mostly required. Discussion, analysis etc. was less predominant. It is to some extent a question of adaption to another system as I appreciated the rigorous introduction to thinkers and philosophies. However, it mostly suited bachelors level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I just mentioned, more repetitive and descriptive - the authority structure between student and teacher is completely different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially the lecture of John Dewey (Mcstravick) and the one concerning the theory of reconnaissance by H. Lorgeril.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were additional lectures, one of which I attended which was very interesting, I would recommend doing that

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend - especially for those living in the CIUP (Cité Universitaire) to go to the trips that are often organized by the different houses. Many are way younger than typical Danish students abroad and the themes and trips can seem somewhat generic but it is a good way to make connections

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: What I just mentioned above, if not, go out and eat and dance in Paris

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The French are different and pretty oriented towards themselves, a bit like Danes, so it is mostly necessary to know the Language and being very active in seeking the company/ attention from others.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go ask anyone from your classes if they wanna hang out. It is not organized in anyway, so a good way to learn how to become very active in searching for new connections

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language mostly and very much the hierarchies between student and teacher.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the wine.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't kid yourself, learn French if you want to study at Sorbonne unless you specifically know that you are going to take English (or whatever other language you might know) classes. 

Don't assume that you will as a natural consequence get new and close connections. Be active and force yourself to be outgoing. 

Be cautious and attentive about the requirements, deadlines etc. academically and administratively. Then everything mostly is solved as the instituion is more flexible than it might seem at a first glance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy a student train card.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The language and the anthropological side of getting acquainted with a completely different way of teaching and interacting - very interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Social connections and building a network in less then 6 months. It is interesting, funny etc. but also tough and at times quite disappointing. However, this is somewhat also the most rewarding thing about the stay, that you can actually stay up even though you do not have your usual social base.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
